children.name: script
children.note: `<script type="text/plain" data-agent-kit-script>` — the spec source, inline (at most one). NOT a schema child part: the element never touches it, and the validator has no rule for script children. The document's own escaping governs; the vocabulary stylesheet promotes the block to a preformatted panel (`themes/_vocabulary.css`, agent-kit section — author origin beats the UA's `script { display: none }`), so BROWSING the page with JavaScript disabled shows the panel unchanged. The `.nojs` build artifact is a different, stricter artifact: its transform strips EVERY `<script>` (hard build invariant), so only there the panel is absent — chips and panel drop, the records do not.

tags.description: Put the spec source inside; the card displays it as written, framed with a script-card header. Reading the source is the point — the card does not run it.
tags.example:

  <script type="text/plain" data-agent-kit-script>
    describe('board', () => { it('mints refs', () => { … }) })
  </script>
</agent-kit-cypress>

<agent-kit-cucumber kind="script" tags="authoring"
                    org="acme" project="semtext" key="feature-extraction">
  <script type="text/plain" data-agent-kit-script>
    Feature: extraction
      Scenario: JS-off equals JS-on
        Given an authored board
        When the records are extracted
        Then both passes agree
  </script>
</agent-kit-cucumber>

tags.summary: A card that shows a Cucumber feature file exactly as written.

attributes.description: required. The agent's identifier, the `⌜<agent-name>` field of the source form. Mirrored to `data-name` after upgrade (the resolved value — an authored `data-name` is never overwritten).
attributes.name: name

attributes.description: required. The agent's archetype (e.g. `scout`, `coder`). Mirrored to `data-type` after upgrade (the resolved value).
attributes.name: type

attributes.description: required. The NPL contract version, the `NPL@{version}` field of the source form. Mirrored to `data-version` after upgrade (the resolved value).
attributes.name: version

attributes.description: optional. The parent agent this definition extends; the header omits it when not authored. Mirrored to `data-extends` after upgrade (the resolved value).
attributes.name: extends

tags.description: You write the agent's name, type, and rules as attributes and text. The page shows them as a tidy card. Machines can read the same fields back.
tags.example:
<npl-agent name="scout" type="scout" version="0.3" extends="base-agent">
Read-only scout: search, read, and summarise; never edit files or run
writes. Report findings with file paths and line numbers.
</npl-agent>
tags.name: npl-agent
tags.summary: Describes one AI agent: its name, type, and how it should behave.

attributes.description: (unset). A content type such as `text`, `code`, `svg`, `markdown`. `svg` routes the content through a sandboxed iframe; every other value (including unset) renders the content preformatted. Mirrored to `data-type` (dual-form contract; the mirror is deferred past parse via afterParse).
attributes.name: type

tags.description: Wrap the artifact's title and content in this element and the page adds a frame around them. The content itself is never changed.
tags.example: Q3 revenue breakdown def q3(): return rows("2026-Q3") Quarterly trend Release note v2.4 ships the viewer M2 lazy opt-in.
tags.name: npl-artifact
tags.summary: Shows a piece of work an agent produced, like code or a report, with a title and notes.

attributes.description: Absent ⇒ the block starts expanded; present ⇒ it starts collapsed. Sets the **initial** open state of the native details; the user's own toggling is never re-forced. The runtime mirrors the boolean to `data-collapsed` (`"true"`/`"false"`) in `updated()` via afterParse — a write for CSS/extraction parity, never an input (the component reads the bare attribute only, like the sem tier's `collapsed`); the mirror is deferred past parse so a sem-source snapshot never sees runtime writes.
attributes.name: collapsed

tags.description: Each step is listed in order, with the final answer at the end. The list uses a plain details box, so it works even with JavaScript off.
tags.example:
Pull the failing test's log lines for the window. The 502s cluster in one 30-second span, not across the hour.
The upstream proxy restarted mid-window; retry, not a code fault.
 Diff the two schema snapshots column by column. Only the column order differs; no column was dropped.
Additive change; safe to migrate without a rollback.
tags.name: npl-cot
tags.summary: Shows the steps of a chain of thought, folded up until the reader opens them.

attributes.description: per the global attribute catalog — optional, the native HTML `id`; the only attribute parameter. No component-specific parameters exist; all content rides the five authored children.
attributes.name: id

children.name: subject
children.note: the thing under critique (one block of content).

children.name: perspective
children.note: the lens the critique is written from (one block).

children.name: strengths
children.note: a list: repeated `item` children (or `li`, or `.npl-item`).

children.name: weaknesses
children.note: a list, same item contract as `strengths`.

children.name: verdict
children.note: the closing judgement (one block; rendered as the highlighted line).

tags.description: You write the subject, the strengths, the weaknesses, and the verdict. The element lays them out as a clean, labelled review card.
tags.example:
<npl-critique id="c1">
  <subject>the launch prompt</subject>
  <perspective>security reviewer</perspective>
  <strengths><item>explicit failure modes</item><item>bounded output</item></strengths>
  <weaknesses><item>no examples</item></weaknesses>
  <verdict>ship after one revision</verdict>
</npl-critique>
tags.name: npl-critique
tags.summary: Shows a review of one thing from one point of view: strengths, weaknesses, and a verdict.

attributes.description: required; a missing version warns and the banner still renders, with the bare mark (`⌜NPL@⌝`). Rendered in the banner mark (`⌜NPL@<version>⌝`) and mirrored to `data-version` (dual-form contract; the mirror is deferred past parse via afterParse so a sem-source snapshot never sees runtime writes).
attributes.name: version

attributes.description: one of `definition` | `extension`. Selects the banner mark (`⌜NPL@…⌝` vs `⌜extend:NPL@…⌝`) and mirrors the resolved kind to `data-type`. Any other value falls back to `definition`.
attributes.name: type

attributes.description: optional; the vocabulary an extension extends, authored on `type="extension"` declarations. Rendered by `.npl-declaration-target` beside the mark whenever authored and mirrored to `data-extend-target` (absent when unauthored).
attributes.name: extend-target

tags.description: It renders the version line of an NPL document, such as NPL@1.0, as a banner at the top. Extended documents are marked the same way.
tags.example:
<npl-declaration version="0.6">Every response states its assumptions before its answer.</npl-declaration>
<npl-declaration version="0.6" type="extension" extend-target="npl-core">This extension adds the session-ledger contract on top of npl-core.</npl-declaration>
tags.name: npl-declaration
tags.summary: Shows which version of a rules document you are reading.

attributes.description: required; the emoji or symbol leading the chip. Rendered by `.npl-directive-glyph` (dropped, gracefully, when absent) and mirrored to `data-glyph` when non-empty.
attributes.name: glyph

attributes.description: one of `directive` | `prefix`. A `prefix` chip renders the `➤` arrow between glyph and instruction, the prefix form's source grammar. Mirrored to `data-kind` (resolved value).
attributes.name: kind

attributes.description: optional; a trailing label beside the instruction, rendered by `.npl-directive-qualifier` and mirrored to `data-qualifier` when non-empty.
attributes.name: qualifier

tags.description: You write the instruction, and optionally a longer note, inside this element. The page shows it as a small chip the reader can spot while scanning.
tags.example:
<npl-directive glyph="🔮" kind="directive" qualifier="style">
  be terse | because the reader is skimming
</npl-directive>
tags.name: npl-directive
tags.summary: Marks a short instruction inside a sentence, so it stands out from the prose.

attributes.description: Displayed by `.npl-example-label` and mirrored to `data-label` (dual-form contract: `data-label` wins when both spellings are present, so the mirror writes the resolved value and never clobbers an authored `data-label`; deferred past parse via afterParse so a sem-source snapshot never sees runtime writes).
attributes.name: label

tags.description: It exists to demonstrate the pattern, not to be used in real documents. Real elements replace it.
tags.example: <npl-example label="hello">authored children survive beside the label</npl-example>
tags.name: npl-example
tags.summary: A sample element that shows how npl-* elements are built.

attributes.description: required, no default. Flag identifier; its wording implies the numeric range checked on `value` (below).
attributes.name: name

attributes.description: no default. Rendered verbatim; validated only when the name implies a numeric range (case-insensitive substring of the name): `freq` checks [0.0, 1.0] (frequency flags), `factor` checks [-10, 10] (hormone factors), `threshold` must be numeric and unbounded. Any other name (pump switches, meta, …) is free-form — never validated. An out-of-range or non-numeric value is NOT an error: the flag renders with the `npl-flag-invalid` warning class on its value span.
attributes.name: value

tags.description: You give it a name and a value. The reader can click the row to apply the setting. If the name implies a number range, values outside it are flagged.
tags.example: <npl-flag name="calm_factor" value="0.5"></npl-flag>
tags.name: npl-flag
tags.summary: One setting a reader can switch, shown as a labelled row.

attributes.description: optional, no default (omit it entirely for no badge). One of `minimal`, `full`, `production`, `creative`, `tireless` (the NPL flag source spells these `preset:<name>`; the attribute accepts the bare word or the prefixed spelling, normalized for display). An unknown preset is NOT an error: it warns through the author-facing channel and renders with the invalid-preset warning class (see Rendered form).
attributes.name: preset

tags.description: It wraps one or more npl-flag elements. You can add a short note above the rows to explain what they do.
tags.example:
<npl-flags preset="production">
  <npl-flag name="calm_factor" value="0.5"></npl-flag>
  tuning notes…
</npl-flags>
tags.name: npl-flags
tags.summary: A group of settings shown as clickable rows.

attributes.description: `panel` renders one row per `h` plus the `state` and `triggered` lines; `bars` renders only the rows (the compact form); `alert` renders only the `alert` elements. Any other value falls back to `panel`.
attributes.name: variant

attributes.description: child element — compound state description, rendered in the `panel` variant as the state line.
attributes.name: state

attributes.description: child element — threshold behaviors activated, or `none`. A row is highlighted (`data-fired`) when this block names the hormone: by symbol (word match, so `RST` does not hit "first"), by name, or by its `trigger` text; `none` highlights nothing.
attributes.name: triggered

attributes.description: child elements — `hormone`, `value`, `threshold`, `behavior` attributes, body text as content. Rendered only by the `alert` variant.
attributes.name: alert

children.name: h
children.note: `<h>` (one per hormone, inside `panel`): `name` (`string`), `symbol` (`string`), `value` (`number`, range [-10, 10] — out-of-range values are clamped into range and the row is marked `data-clamped`, the raw text mirrored to `data-value`), `delta` (`number`; the sign drives the arrow: positive up `↑`, negative down `↓`, zero or absent flat `→`), `trigger` (`string`).

tags.description: Each drive has a level from 0 to 100, drawn as a bar with an arrow showing whether it rose or fell. Notes explain what a bar means when it passes a set limit.
tags.example:
<npl-hormones variant="panel">
  <panel>
    <h name="Momentum"     symbol="MTM" value="6"   delta="+2" trigger="Tests passed first try"></h>
    <h name="Tension"      symbol="TNS" value="3"   delta="0"  trigger="Complexity"></h>
    <h name="Restlessness" symbol="RST" value="8.5" delta="-1" trigger="Strategy failed"></h>
  </panel>
  <state>Productive tension</state>
  <triggered>RST threshold crossed</triggered>
  <alert hormone="RST" value="8.5" threshold="7" behavior="strategy-switch">
    Restlessness threshold crossed. Initiating plan-of-action.
  </alert>
</npl-hormones>
tags.name: npl-hormones
tags.summary: Shows seven drive levels — like momentum, tension, and curiosity — as bars.

children.name: npl-intent-overview
children.note: the goal: what the effort is trying to do.

children.name: npl-intent-scope
children.note: what is in and out of scope.

children.name: npl-intent-outcomes
children.note: what success looks like.

children.name: npl-intent-assumptions
children.note: the assumptions grid.

children.name: npl-intent-assumption
children.note: one assumption row inside the grid; its statement is the authored text, plus one optional parameter, `confidence`: string — default `—`. Rendered into the grid's second column; either spelling, `data-confidence` wins.

tags.description: You write the goal, what is in and out of scope, the outcomes, and any assumptions. The element lays them out in a clear grid so a reader can check the plan at a glance.
tags.example:
Ship the fleet dashboard to stage. Metrics only; no alerting yet.
  • One pane per service
 SigNoz keeps serving uptime queries. The chart repo stays ArgoCD-watched. ArgoCD auto-syncs from the chart repo.
tags.name: npl-intent
tags.summary: Shows what a piece of work is meant to achieve: the goal, the scope, and the expected outcomes.

attributes.description: optional, a theory-of-mind reading is a guess until corrected; authored `0..1`. Out-of-range values are **clamped** into `[0,1]` (a non-numeric authoring clamps to `0`), and the host is **marked**: `data-confidence` carries the clamped value, `data-confidence-out-of-range` the verbatim authored value, and the meter gains a `npl-mindread-confidence-out` note.
attributes.name: confidence

tags.description: You write the subject, the signals (tone, patterns, things left unsaid), and the reading drawn from them. The result is clearly labelled as a guess, not a fact.
tags.example:
<npl-mindread confidence="0.7">
  <subject>User</subject>
  <signals><signal type="tone">Terse fragments — formality dropped.</signal></signals>
  <inferred>
    <motive>Quick resolution over thoroughness.</motive>
    <mood>😤 Pressured, time-crunched</mood>
    <cognitive>Execution mode — solutions, not options.</cognitive>
    <unspoken>Reassurance that it'll be ready.</unspoken>
  </inferred>
  <adaptation>Working solution first; edge cases deferred. Short replies.</adaptation>
</npl-mindread>
tags.name: npl-mindread
tags.summary: Shows what one party thinks another party believes or feels.

attributes.description: Resolved in either authoring spelling (`data-primary` wins, conventions §2). Declares this the primary lens; marks the rendered chips (`npl-mode-chip-primary`) and mirrors to `data-primary` after parse — an authored `data-primary` is never clobbered by the default.
attributes.name: primary

children.name: mode
children.note: `type`: `string` — required. The lens name; the chip's label. A `mode` without `type` is skipped.

tags.description: You write each mode as a child element. The main mode is marked so the reader knows which lens leads. This element only shows information; it changes nothing.
tags.example:
<npl-mode>
  <mode type="planner"></mode>
  <mode type="executing"></mode>
</npl-mode>
tags.name: npl-mode
tags.summary: Lists the thinking styles an agent uses, one chip per style.

attributes.description: required. One emoji followed by an optional qualifier string, whitespace-separated (`"🙂 wistful"`); a lone emoji is valid. Displayed by `.npl-mood-chip` and mirrored to `data-mood` (dual-form contract; the mirror is deferred past parse via afterParse so a sem-source snapshot never sees runtime writes).
attributes.name: mood

children.name: npl-mood-tone
children.note: how the affect colors delivery.

children.name: npl-mood-context
children.note: what the mood attaches to.

children.name: npl-mood-approach
children.note: the stance the mood implies going forward.

tags.description: You write the mood in the mood attribute. Extra children can carry the tone, the context, and how the agent will approach work in this mood.
tags.example:
restrained, unhurried
draft reply to a cold opener
ask one concrete question
tags.name: npl-mood
tags.summary: Shows a mood with an emoji, plus an optional note on its tone.

attributes.description: One of `lr` | `td`; declares the intended flow and mirrors to `data-direction` (dual-form contract, `data-` wins, mirror deferred past parse via afterParse). The fence's own `graph LR`/`graph TD` line remains the renderer's source of truth — authored source is never rewritten. Anything other than `lr`/`td` falls back to `lr` with an author-facing warning.
attributes.name: direction

tags.description: You write the tree, the reasoning with weights, and the option that was picked. The element shows all three parts; it never draws the tree for you.
tags.example:
graph LR
  A{Decision} -->|"90%"| B[Path B]
  A -->|"40%"| C[Path C]
A --[90%]--> B: why this path is weighted high A --[40%]--> C: why this is less preferred Path B — 90% weight; lowest migration cost.
tags.name: npl-poa
tags.summary: Shows a plan as a decision tree, plus the reasons each path was weighed.

attributes.description: one of `full`, `compact`, optional — `full` renders each section as a labelled block; `compact` renders one emoji line per section. Any other value resolves to `full`, and the resolved variant mirrors to `data-variant` (dual-form contract; the mirror is deferred past parse via afterParse, like sem-note, so a sem-source snapshot never sees runtime writes). The variant is read at upgrade; it is display-only and not switched after wiring.
attributes.name: variant

children.name: assessment
children.note: what held and what did not across the finished turn.

children.name: improvements
children.note: concrete changes the next run should carry.

children.name: validation
children.note: how the result was checked.

children.name: eval
children.note: the measured outcome (scores, counts, diffs).

children.name: fine-tune
children.note: training or retrieval follow-ups.

tags.description: You write the assessment, the improvements, the validation, and any eval notes. The element lays them out as a review card after the work.
tags.example:
<npl-ref variant="full">
  <assessment>the approach held; one gap in the eval loop</assessment>
  <improvements>add a regression harness before the next run</improvements>
  <validation>checked against three traces</validation>
  <eval>quality 0.82 vs 0.71 baseline</eval>
  <fine-tune>retrain on the two rejected traces</fine-tune>
</npl-ref>
tags.name: npl-ref
tags.summary: Looks back at a finished turn: what went well, what to improve, and how it was checked.

attributes.description: (empty). Rendered as the table caption and mirrored to `data-title` (dual-form contract; the mirror is deferred past parse via afterParse so a sem-source snapshot never sees runtime writes).
attributes.name: title

attributes.description: (optional, one) — `value`: number — default: the element's trimmed text (`value` wins when both are present). States the overall score; when absent or non-numeric the component computes the weighted average — sum(weight · score) ÷ sum(weight) over the criteria with a numeric weight AND score (all-zero weights ⇒ no figure).
attributes.name: npl-overall-score

tags.description: You write the criteria, their weights, and their scores. The total is shown as given, or worked out from the weights. Wrong or missing numbers are flagged, not hidden.
tags.example:
<npl-rubric title="Code review">
  <npl-criterion name="Correctness" weight="3" score="4"></npl-criterion>
  <npl-criterion name="Style" weight="1" score="5"></npl-criterion>
  <npl-overall-score value="4.2"></npl-overall-score>
</npl-rubric>
tags.name: npl-rubric
tags.summary: A scoring table: each row is a criterion with a weight and a score, plus a total.

attributes.description: required. One of the known section types: `alg`, `alg-pseudo`, `diagram`, `example`, `format`, `logic`, `note`, `syntax`, `template`.
attributes.name: type

tags.description: Known section types get a matching header; unknown types get a warning style so a typo is easy to spot. The content stays plain text, so search and copy still work.
tags.example: section := "<npl-section" type ">" body "</npl-section>"
tags.name: npl-section
tags.summary: A labelled section for any NPL prompt block.

attributes.description: optional; One of the eleven NPL thought-block types (case-insensitive): `observation`, `tangent`, `question`, `relation`, `concern`, `affirmation`, `reflection`, `opportunity`, `aversion`, `interest`, `eval`.
attributes.name: type

tags.description: Each child is one thought with a type attribute, such as a question or a risk. The element shows them as a tidy list of bubbles.
tags.example:
<npl-thought id="t1">
  <npl-thought type="observation">The cache misses cluster on Mondays.</npl-thought>
  <npl-thought type="tangent">Mondays are also the fleet redeploy window…</npl-thought>
  <npl-thought type="balloon">unknown — degrades to plain text</npl-thought>
  <npl-thought>no type — a sub-container; its children survive untouched</npl-thought>
</npl-thought>
tags.name: npl-thought
tags.summary: A thought bubble: short related ideas grouped under one type.

attributes.description: One of `entry`, `exit`; rendered as the bracket label and mirrored to data-phase (dual-form contract; the mirror is deferred past parse via afterParse so a sem-source snapshot never sees runtime writes).
attributes.name: phase

tags.description: You write each part of the state. The element shows them as labelled parts of one bracket. An optional collective part covers group personas.
tags.example:
raw impulse — what the first instinct wants to do

reality-tested approach — what is actually done and why

🔥 — energized by the profiling work

internalized standards — what should be upheld here

system-level observation from outside the persona
tags.name: npl-vos
tags.summary: Shows a persona's inner state: id, ego, superego, and mood, before a reply.

tags.description: You wrap the words to remember in a highlight child, or use [[double brackets]] as shorthand. Hiding them turns the passage into a self-test; showing them again reveals the answers.
tags.example:
<sem-details id="oidc-docs">
  <sem-detail>
    The OIDC token travels in the
    <highlight>Authorization</highlight> header.
  </sem-detail>
</sem-details>
tags.name: highlight
tags.summary: Prose with parts the reader can hide to test their recall.

attributes.description: (on `sem-api-call`): required, string — the operation's display name.
attributes.name: name

attributes.description: (optional): string token — HTTP method, rendered uppercased, extraction records the authored spelling uppercased.
attributes.name: method

attributes.description: (optional): string — the documented response status ("200", "2xx", "201 Created" …).
attributes.name: status

tags.description: The definition card for an endpoint. You write the operation name, HTTP method and path, then one sem-api-param child per parameter or response field; the page shows a table and machines read the same fields back.
tags.example:
<sem-api-call name="Create token" method="POST" endpoint="/oauth/token" status="200">
  Exchanges a grant for a token pair.
  <sem-api-param name="grant_type" in="body" type="string" required allowed="authorization_code,refresh_token">The grant to exchange.</sem-api-param>
  <sem-api-param name="code" in="body" type="string">The authorization code.</sem-api-param>
  <sem-api-param name="ttl" in="response" type="integer">Access-token lifetime in seconds.</sem-api-param>

tags.description: You write tables, lists, and other Markdown inside the element. Readers see a formatted table or list; machines get the Markdown back unchanged. Made for content that is easier to write as Markdown than as HTML.

<sem-md id="m-lifetimes" label="Token lifetimes" controls="toggle,copy">
  | Token   | Lifetime | Rotates |
  | :------ | -------: | :-----: |

  | refresh | 30 days  | yes     |
</sem-md>
tags.name: sem-md
tags.summary: A block written in Markdown that the browser turns into HTML.

attributes.description: one of `text` (default), `html` — presentation selector; display-only sugar.
attributes.name: mode

attributes.description: optional qualifier drawn into the label chrome.
attributes.name: kind

tags.description: Pick text or html mode and put the mockup inside. The card frames it as a draft visual, clearly not a live interface.
tags.name: sem-mockup
tags.summary: A design mockup container: text or HTML shown as a picture of a UI.

attributes.description: boolean attr — the body is hidden behind a ten-word teaser (`.sem-note-summary`) that expands on click.
attributes.name: collapsed

attributes.description: presentation only. On wide viewports the note floats right beside the prose that follows it (width `--sem-margin-width`, default 14rem), inside the container; a document whose column has a gutter pushes it out with `--sem-margin-offset`. On narrow viewports and in print it reads inline as an ordinary callout. CSS-only — no handler, no chrome, no record change.
attributes.name: view-as

tags.description: Pick a variant — info, warning, tip, or danger — for the colour and label. The collapsed attribute hides the body behind a short teaser. It stays ordinary readable text with JavaScript off.
tags.example:
<sem-note variant="warning">The migration job expects the MinIO port-forward on 127.0.0.1:9000 — start it before you apply.</sem-note>
<sem-note variant="tip" collapsed>Snapshot the volume first; once the rotation job starts, the old keys are gone for good.</sem-note>
tags.name: sem-note
tags.summary: A callout: a short piece of prose set beside the main text.

attributes.description: optional qualifier drawn into the label chrome (display-only sugar).
attributes.name: kind

tags.description: Write the principles as prose or sections inside; the container adds a labeled frame and nothing more.
tags.example: Velocity-first, integrity-absolute: ship aggressively, never gamble data.

attributes.description: optional qualifier drawn into the label chrome (display-only sugar).
attributes.name: kind

attributes.description: per the global catalog (`done`, `current`, `todo`, `blocked`, `pass`, `fail`) — drawn as a status chip (display-only).
attributes.name: status

tags.description: Write the plan as sections or prose inside. A status attribute tracks where the plan stands, and the container adds a labeled frame.
tags.example:
1. Snapshot the current chart tag.

2. Land the rotation fix behind the release train.

3. Confirm the pod image, not just ArgoCD sync.
tags.name: sem-plan
tags.summary: A plan container: the approach and its reasoning in one place.

tags.description: You write one sem-step per step, in the order they happen. Each step carries a status: done, current, todo, or blocked. There are no step numbers to maintain — position is the number.
tags.example:
<sem-procedure kind="runbook" role="list">
  <sem-step role="listitem" status="done">provision Infisical path</sem-step>
  <sem-step role="listitem" status="current">port-forward MinIO</sem-step>
  <sem-step role="listitem">run migrations</sem-step>
  <sem-step role="listitem" status="blocked">cut release — waiting on CI</sem-step>
</sem-procedure>
tags.name: sem-procedure
tags.summary: An ordered list of steps, each marked with where it stands.

tags.description: You give it an id and a short label. Sections tagged with this id show or hide as the reader switches groups.
tags.example:
<sem-audiences>
  <sem-profile id="reader" label="Reader"></sem-profile>
  <sem-profile id="operator" label="Operator" implies="reader"></sem-profile>
</sem-audiences>
tags.name: sem-profile
tags.summary: Names one reader group inside a sem-audiences block.

attributes.description: required, canonical unit 0..1. Out-of-range values clamp for rendering; the raw attr stays untouched (machine readers see the author's value, the render shows the clamp).
attributes.name: value

attributes.description: optional completion state — pairs with value 1 and renders the full/accent state (same catalog as `sem-step`).
attributes.name: status

tags.description: You give it a value and an optional label. The page draws a bar with the percentage. Values outside the range are clamped for display, and the raw value still reads as text without JavaScript.
tags.example:
<sem-progress value="0.62" label="coverage"
     role="meter" aria-valuemin="0" aria-valuemax="1" aria-valuenow="0.62"></sem-progress>
tags.name: sem-progress
tags.summary: A progress bar for one number between 0 and 1.

attributes.description: (on each `sem-property`): required, free text (the term). The property text is the value.
attributes.name: key

attributes.description: (optional; R/W1): the block is a glossary. Each property should carry an `id`; prose elsewhere links a term with a plain anchor (`JWT`), optionally wrapping it in `` at its defining use.
attributes.name: view-as

tags.description: You write one sem-property per pair. The grid renders with plain CSS, so it works with JavaScript off. Machines read the same pairs back.
tags.example:
<sem-properties kind="config">
  <sem-property key="token ttl" role="definition" aria-label="token ttl">15m</sem-property>
  <sem-property key="refresh rotation" role="definition" aria-label="refresh rotation">per use</sem-property>
  <sem-property key="storage" role="definition" aria-label="storage">httpOnly cookie</sem-property>
</sem-properties>
tags.name: sem-properties
tags.summary: A list of key–value pairs, shown as a tidy definition grid.

tags.description: The key attribute is the term; the text inside is its meaning. Add role=definition when the value defines the key.
tags.example:
<sem-properties kind="config">
  <sem-property key="token ttl" role="definition" aria-label="token ttl">15m</sem-property>
  <sem-property key="refresh rotation" role="definition" aria-label="refresh rotation">per use</sem-property>
  <sem-property key="storage" role="definition" aria-label="storage">httpOnly cookie</sem-property>
</sem-properties>
tags.name: sem-property
tags.summary: One key–value pair in a properties grid.

attributes.description: optional. Comma flags, in any order, one of `outline`, `progress`, `focus`, `type`, `color`, `print`, `audience` — unknown flags, including the theme flag reserved for R/W3, are ignored. Controls render in the **canonical order** above, not in attribute order.
attributes.name: controls

attributes.description: optional. Deepest heading level in the generated outline, `2`–`6`; The outline always starts at `h2` — `h1` is the document title.
attributes.name: outline-depth

children.name: nav
children.note: Child (optional): an authored `<nav aria-label="Contents">`. When present it is the outline, **used verbatim** — no ids are assigned, no list is generated, nothing inside it is rewritten. This is the JS-off table of contents.

tags.description: It is page furniture, not content — a document without it loses nothing a machine would read. Readers get focus mode, type size, colour scheme, print, and audience controls in one place.
tags.example: <sem-reader controls="outline,progress,focus,type,color,print,audience" outline-depth="3"></sem-reader>
tags.name: sem-reader
tags.summary: Reading tools for a long document: an outline, a progress bar, and controls for text size and theme.

tags.description: You give it an id, a link, and a note. In the text, cite it with a plain link to the id. The element carries the fields a plain list item cannot.
tags.example:
Rotate refresh tokens per use[1].

The OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework, §10.4. A footnote with no external target.
tags.name: sem-reference
tags.summary: One numbered entry in a reference list.

attributes.description: `footnotes` | `bibliography` (free token; these two get distinct styling). Optional.
attributes.name: kind

attributes.description: (required; on each `sem-reference`): the citation target — the global `id`.
attributes.name: id

attributes.description: (optional; on each `sem-reference`): external location (`data-href` in the class form).
attributes.name: href

tags.description: You wrap one sem-reference per source. Numbers come from position. With JavaScript off the list still reads as an ordinary numbered list.
tags.example:
Rotate refresh tokens per use[1].

The OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework, §10.4. A footnote with no external target.
tags.name: sem-references
tags.summary: A numbered list of sources the document cites.

attributes.description: one of `functional`, `non-functional`, `constraint` — the requirement class, drawn into the label chrome.
attributes.name: kind

attributes.description: one of `draft`, `approved`, `implemented` — lifecycle token, drawn as a status chip (display-only).
attributes.name: status

attributes.description: free token (e.g. `high`); drawn into the status chip when present.
attributes.name: priority

tags.description: Mark it functional, non-functional, or a constraint; a status and priority travel with it. The container keeps the statement readable while the classification stays machine-readable.
tags.example:
<sem-requirement id="req-session-rotate" kind="functional"
  status="approved" priority="high">
  Access tokens MUST rotate at most 15 minutes after issue.
</sem-requirement>
tags.name: sem-requirement
tags.summary: One requirement, stated plainly and classified.

attributes.description: optional label for the closed state. Default: the leading body text (max 60 chars, cut at the last word boundary, trailing punctuation dropped) acts as summary when absent.
attributes.name: summary

attributes.description: boolean attr — starts **revealed** (no control; the body is live immediately; the host carries `data-revealed`).
attributes.name: open

attributes.description: boolean attr — accepted, no-op. Hidden is the default.
attributes.name: collapsed

tags.description: You write the question as the summary and the answer as the body. It is a plain details box, so it works with JavaScript off. Use it for explanation — a sem-fact is for claims.
tags.example:
<sem-reveal summary="Why not localStorage?">
  Tokens in localStorage are readable by any script on the page…
</sem-reveal>
tags.name: sem-reveal
tags.summary: A question the reader clicks to reveal the answer.

attributes.description: the scale ceiling (minimum 0); drawn into the label chrome as a chip when present.
attributes.name: max-score

tags.description: Author the grid as a plain table or row prose inside; the container does not force a shape. A max-score attribute records the top of the scale.
tags.example:
criterion0510
accuracywrongpartialexact

tags.summary: A scoring rubric: criteria and levels laid out as a grid.

attributes.description: optional qualifier drawn into the label chrome (display-only sugar).
attributes.name: kind

attributes.description: `any` — per the global catalog (`sem-audiences`); the runbook itself does no audience gating, the document profiles do.
attributes.name: audience

tags.description: Author preconditions, procedure, and references with the elements you already have; the container adds chrome and a label. An audience attribute says who it is for.
tags.example:
Preconditions: port-forward to the admin DB.

Snapshot the current chart tag. Bump and deploy.
tags.name: sem-runbook
tags.summary: An operational runbook: what to check before, what to do, and what to read next.

children.name: mode
children.note: `structured` (default) | `text`; text selects the pre-form parse (see sem-file-tree.md — the same dispatch serves both tags).

tags.description: Each node carries a path with an optional label and kind; the card draws the hierarchy. Prefer this over typing a text tree when you want structure a machine can read back.

<sem-site-tree label="Monorepo layout">
  <node path="src" label="Source" kind="dir">
    <node path="src/lit" kind="dir" collapsed>
      <node path="src/lit/sem-workflow.ts" kind="file"></node>
      <node path="src/lit/sem-tree.ts" kind="file"></node>
    </node>
  </node>
  <node path="themes" kind="dir"></node>
</sem-site-tree>
tags.name: sem-site-tree
tags.summary: A site or file tree authored as real nested nodes.

attributes.description: `html` (default) | `source`. The initial mode. Mutable presentation: the toggle rewrites `data-view-as` at runtime (the authored bare attribute is left alone), and extraction ignores it (spec/extraction.md §5c).
attributes.name: view-as

attributes.description: (optional): a short caption rendered in the chrome.
attributes.name: label

tags.description: You put ordinary SemText inside. The reader sees the rendered result, then the exact source that produced it. Made for documents that teach the vocabulary.
tags.example:
Facts — flashcards

SemText snapshots the section before enhancement The fence shows the parsed markup, never the file bytes.

tags.summary: Lets the reader flip between a section as it renders and the markup behind it.

children.name: sem-step
children.note: status: `done` | `current` | `todo` (default) | `blocked`.

tags.description: You write the instruction as the text and set status to done, current, todo, or blocked. Its place in the page is its order in the procedure.
tags.example:
<sem-procedure kind="runbook" role="list">
  <sem-step role="listitem" status="done">provision Infisical path</sem-step>
  <sem-step role="listitem" status="current">port-forward MinIO</sem-step>
  <sem-step role="listitem">run migrations</sem-step>

</sem-procedure>

attributes.description: optional qualifier drawn into the label chrome (display-only sugar).
attributes.name: kind

tags.description: Put the gist inside; the container frames it as a summary readers can skim before the full text.
tags.example: Tokens rotate per session; secrets never reach the browser; the client mints fresh pairs from the refresh grant.
tags.name: sem-summary
tags.summary: A short summary block set at the top of longer content.

attributes.description: (optional, on `<td>`): the sort key for that cell when the visible text is not the key (`15 min` vs `900`). Two numeric keys compare numerically; anything else compares as text, locale-aware.
attributes.name: data-value

attributes.description: (optional): one of the comma flags `sort`, `filter`; Unknown flags are ignored.
attributes.name: controls

attributes.description: (boolean, optional): the header row sticks to the top of the scroll container. Opting in also caps the element at `max-height: 24rem` so a long table scrolls inside itself — the stick needs an internal scroll container to engage, and without it a page-level table never gains one and the header would scroll away like any other row. CSS only — works with scripts off.
attributes.name: sticky

children.name: table
children.note: Child: **exactly one `<table>`**, holding exactly one thead (its first row: header cells carrying `scope="col"`), one tbody, and optionally a caption first. A table without a thead gets no sort control. Anything else inside the table — tfoot, colgroup — is left alone.

tags.description: You write a normal HTML table. Sorting and filtering only change what the reader sees; the markup stays the contract, so machines always read the same rows you wrote.
tags.example:
Token lifetimes
TokenLifetimeRotates
access15 minno
device7 daysyes
refresh30 daysyes
tags.name: sem-table
tags.summary: A table the reader can sort and filter — the table you write is the data.

tags.description: The child of sem-tag-def. You write the attribute's name and type, add the required flag when it must be present, and the description text is what readers see in that row.
tags.example:
<sem-tag-def tag="sem-note" name="Note" group="annotation"
             children="sem-note-body sem-note-summary">
  An inline annotation with an optional variant and a collapsible body.
  <sem-tag-attr name="variant" type="string" allowed="tip,warning,danger" default="tip">Display variant.</sem-tag-attr>
  <sem-tag-attr name="collapsed" type="boolean">Starts hidden.</sem-tag-attr>
</sem-tag-def>
tags.name: sem-tag-attr
tags.summary: One attribute row inside a sem-tag-def: name, type, required flag, default and description.

attributes.description: (on `sem-tag-def`): required, string — the documented tag's name (backtick-free, strict tag shape).
attributes.name: tag

attributes.description: (optional): string — human display name ("Note") when it differs from the tag name.
attributes.name: name

attributes.description: (optional): free token — grouping label for reference indexes (`annotation`, `layout`, `data` …).
attributes.name: group

attributes.description: (optional): comma/space token list — the documented tag's child tags.
attributes.name: children

tags.description: The definition card for a markup tag. You write the tag name and one sem-tag-attr child per attribute; the page shows a tidy table and machines read the same fields back. The reference pages use it, so the vocabulary documents itself.
tags.example:
<sem-tag-def tag="sem-note" name="Note" group="annotation"
             children="sem-note-body sem-note-summary">
  An inline annotation with an optional variant and a collapsible body.
  <sem-tag-attr name="variant" type="string" allowed="tip,warning,danger" default="tip">Display variant.</sem-tag-attr>
  <sem-tag-attr name="collapsed" type="boolean">Starts hidden.</sem-tag-attr>
</sem-tag-def>
tags.name: sem-tag-def
tags.summary: Documents one tag's contract: its attributes, types, defaults and child tags, as a card.

attributes.description: optional methodology qualifier drawn into the label chrome (display-only sugar).
attributes.name: kind

attributes.description: free token naming the modelled boundary; drawn into the label chrome when present.
attributes.name: scope

tags.description: Author them as sections or list-style prose inside; the container adds chrome and a label. A scope attribute says what the model covers.
tags.example:
Assets

Session tokens; the Infisical-backed secret store.

Mitigations

Tokens rotate per session; secrets never reach the browser.
tags.name: sem-threat-model
tags.summary: A threat model: the assets, threats, and mitigations in one container.

tags.description: Whatever you put inside is the whole record — the reader skims it or skips it. The container keeps it visually separate from the body.
tags.example:
<sem-tldr id="t-auth">
  Rotate JWTs per session; keep refresh tokens server-side.
</sem-tldr>
tags.name: sem-tldr
tags.summary: A too-long-didn't-read block: the whole point in a few lines.

tags.description: Use it inside a troubleshooting collection. The entry stays ordinary structured text a reader can scan.
tags.example:
<sem-tsgs id="tsg-deploy" kind="deploys">
  <sem-tsg>
    <name>stale-image</name>
    <title>Pod serves the old image after a green sync</title>
    <description>ArgoCD reports Synced/Healthy but the rollout
    did not change.</description>
    <tags>deploy, argocd</tags>
    <when>right after a release merge</when>
    Confirm the pod image spec per container — Synced/Healthy alone
    can serve a stale image.
  </sem-tsg>
  <sem-tsg>
    <name>port-forward</name>
    <title>Admin MinIO unreachable for terragrunt</title>
    Port-forward 127.0.0.1:9000 before any --all run.
  </sem-tsg>
</sem-tsgs>
tags.name: sem-tsg
tags.summary: One entry in a troubleshooting guide: symptom, cause, fix.

attributes.description: collection qualifier drawn into the label chrome (display-only sugar).
attributes.name: kind

tags.description: Wrap your entries in it and the page lays them out consistently. Each entry pairs a problem with its resolution in plain text.
tags.example:
<sem-tsgs id="tsg-deploy" kind="deploys">
  <sem-tsg>

    <title>Pod serves the old image after a green sync</title>
    <description>ArgoCD reports Synced/Healthy but the rollout
    did not change.</description>
    <tags>deploy, argocd</tags>
    <when>right after a release merge</when>
    Confirm the pod image spec per container — Synced/Healthy alone
    can serve a stale image.
  </sem-tsg>
  <sem-tsg>
    <name>port-forward</name>
    <title>Admin MinIO unreachable for terragrunt</title>
    Port-forward 127.0.0.1:9000 before any --all run.
  </sem-tsg>
</sem-tsgs>
tags.name: sem-tsgs
tags.summary: A collection of troubleshooting guides.

tags.description: The name attribute labels the tab; the content inside is that view of the subject. With JavaScript off every view shows, each under its name.
tags.example:
<sem-views id="deploy">
  <sem-view name="Helm" active>content…</sem-view>
  <sem-view name="ArgoCD">content…</sem-view>
</sem-views>
tags.name: sem-view
tags.summary: One named perspective inside a sem-views tab set.

attributes.description: required, unique within the container, human label.
attributes.name: name

attributes.description: boolean marker on the initially-visible view; **if no view carries it, the first view is active**. The shown view is tracked at runtime in `data-active` (the component mirrors an authored `active` there, then moves it on every switch); the authored attribute is never rewritten.
attributes.name: active

attributes.description: required **for enhancement, not only for deep links** — the handler selects `.sem-views[id]`, so a container without an id never upgrades and stays stacked (the JS-off form) even with script running. Also the deep-link head (`#deploy/argocd`); `kind`, `tags` global.
attributes.name: id

tags.description: You wrap sem-view children and name each one. Readers switch by click, keyboard, or link. The content is never moved or rewritten — only which view shows changes.
tags.example:
<sem-views id="deploy">
  <sem-view name="Helm" active>content…</sem-view>
  <sem-view name="ArgoCD">content…</sem-view>
</sem-views>
tags.name: sem-views
tags.summary: Shows one subject several ways, with a tab bar to switch.

children.name: duration
children.note: free token (`45m`, `2h` …); whole-workflow estimate.

tags.description: Author sem-step children in order; a step can say how to verify it and what to do when the check fails. Durations travel with steps where you know them.
tags.example:
<sem-workflow kind="release" duration="45m" label="Cut a release">
  <sem-step id="s1" action="Build images" description="sha-tagged via CI"
    gate="CI green" check="gh run view" output="dist/*.tar">push the tag</sem-step>
  <sem-step id="s2" action="Deploy stage" gate="images present"
    check="gh-wait deploy" if-no="fix CI, then re-run the release workflow">merge to stage</sem-step>
</sem-workflow>
tags.name: sem-workflow
tags.summary: An ordered workflow whose steps carry checks and failure paths.
